diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-1 Crankcase emission control system
diagrams.description: Cross-sectional cutaway diagram showing crankcase ventilation gas flow routes with P.C.V. valve detail under partial and full throttle conditions.
wiring_and_connections: Ventilation hose between throttle chamber and rocker cover
Hose between crankcase and P.C.V. valve to intake manifold
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Ensure that flame arrester is surely inserted in hose between throttle chamber and rocker cover. Check for hissing sound and strong vacuum at P.C.V. valve inlet at idle.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-2 Location of emission control system components
diagrams.description: Phantom vehicle perspective showing layout and locations of all major emission control and EFI components on the Datsun 280Z chassis and engine bay.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Shows component locations throughout vehicle including under-hood EFI components, chassis underbody catalytic converter, and passenger cabin / rear fuel system elements.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-3 Schematic drawing of B.C.D.D.
diagrams.description: Internal pneumatic cutaway and electrical control schematic of the B.C.D.D. unit showing Non-California and California altitude corrector configurations.

callouts.3: Speed detecting switch Below 16 km/h (10 MPH): ON (For M/T)
callouts.4: Inhibitor switch \"N\" or \"P\" position: ON (For A/T)

measurements_and_specs: Speed detecting switch closes below 16 km/h (10 MPH)
wiring_and_connections: Ignition switch to amplifier and solenoid valve
Speed detecting switch (M/T) to amplifier
Inhibitor switch (A/T) circuit
diagrams.mechanic_notes: California model incorporates altitude corrector with adjusting nut and lock spring; Non-California model utilizes adjusting screw.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-4 Removing B.C.D.D.
diagrams.description: Illustration of the underside of the throttle chamber indicating which three screws to remove and cautioning against removing the four assembly screws.
measurements_and_specs: Securing screws tightening torque: 20 to 40 kg-cm (17 to 35 in-lb)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Do not unscrew the four B.C.D.D. assembly screws (2). Replace B.C.D.D. as an assembly if malfunctioning.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-5 Checking B.C.D.D. circuit with function test connector (for manual transmission)
diagrams.description: Wiring test diagram and multimeter hookup to terminals A and B of the function test connector for manual transmission vehicles.

callouts.4: Speed detecting switch (Above 10 mph: OFF / Below 10 mph: ON)

wiring_and_connections: Terminals A and B of function test connector
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Do not attach test leads to terminals other than designated A and B.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-6 Checking B.C.D.D. circuit with function test connector (for automatic transmission)
diagrams.description: Circuit schematic and tester connection diagram for testing B.C.D.D. via the test connector on automatic transmission models.

callouts.2: Inhibitor switch (N or P position: ON / 1, 2, D or R position: OFF)

measurements_and_specs: Voltage in N or P: 12 V (d-c)
Resistance in gear (1, 2, D, R): 15 to 28 ohms
wiring_and_connections: Terminals A and B of function test connector
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Check for 12V in N/P and 15 to 28 ohms in drive/reverse ranges across terminals A and B.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-7 Checking solenoid valve
diagrams.description: Connecting jumper test wire from battery positive terminal to the disconnected B.C.D.D. solenoid valve harness connector to listen for valve click.
wiring_and_connections: Intermittent electrification to solenoid terminal
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Turn on ignition key without starting engine, ensure solenoid clicks when energized.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-8 Checking amplifier
diagrams.description: Circuit schematic showing ammeter connection between ignition key circuit and amplifier to test current draw upon key turn-on.

callouts.3: Speed detecting switch (Above 16 km/h / 10 MPH: OFF, Below 16 km/h / 10 MPH: ON)

measurements_and_specs: Tester range: DC ampere (1A min full scale)
wiring_and_connections: Test probes in series with amplifier circuit
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Do not confuse positive line with negative line. Tester needle should deflect when ignition is switched ON.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-9 Removing harness of solenoid valve
diagrams.description: Disconnecting the electrical plug harness from the B.C.D.D. vacuum control solenoid valve on the throttle chamber.
wiring_and_connections: Solenoid harness connector disconnected
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Always disconnect solenoid harness prior to performing B.C.D.D. operating pressure check or adjustment.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-10 Connecting vacuum gauge
diagrams.description: Vacuum gauge connection via rubber hose tee to the intake manifold vacuum fitting.
measurements_and_specs: Quick-response Bourdon type boost gauge recommended
wiring_and_connections: Rubber vacuum hose to intake manifold fitting
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Use Bourdon tube boost gauge for fast response during rapid throttle snapping.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-11 Adjusting operating pressure (California models)
diagrams.description: Adjusting the B.C.D.D. operating pressure on California models using a wrench on the adjusting nut through the lock spring.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Turn adjusting nut in or out with lock spring in place. Always set lock spring properly to prevent drift in operating pressure.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-12 Adjusting operating pressure (Non-California models)
diagrams.description: Cross-section and screwdriver adjustment of the B.C.D.D. operating pressure adjusting screw on Non-California models.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Turn adjusting screw counterclockwise if operating pressure is lower than set level. Clockwise turn decreases vacuum setting.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-13 Changes in operating pressure versus changes in atmospheric pressure and altitude (California models)
diagrams.description: Engineering graph plotting operating vacuum of B.C.D.D. (mmHg and inHg) against atmospheric pressure and altitude in thousands of feet and kilometers.
components: Operating vacuum scale (300 to 600 mmHg / 12 to 24 inHg)
Atmospheric pressure scale (450 to 750 mmHg / 18 to 30 inHg)
Altitude scale (0 to 6000 ft / 0 to 2.0 km)

callouts.A: Arrow line tracing from atmospheric pressure

diagrams.mechanic_notes: Use trace line A when atmospheric pressure is known, trace line B when altitude is known.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-14 E.G.R. control system
diagrams.description: Functional schematic diagram of the complete E.G.R. circuit showing routing between intake manifold, throttle chamber, E.G.R. valve, B.P.T. valve, thermal vacuum valve, and exhaust manifold.
measurements_and_specs: Operating range: water temp 50 to 95°C (122 to 203°F)
B.P.T. valve exhaust threshold: 21 to 33 mmH2O (0.82 to 1.30 inH2O)
wiring_and_connections: Vacuum lines between throttle chamber, thermal vacuum valve, B.P.T. valve, and E.G.R. control valve
Exhaust pressure sensing line to B.P.T. valve
diagrams.mechanic_notes: E.G.R. is deactivated at idle and full throttle. California models include vacuum delay valve (8).

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-15 E.G.R. control valve
diagrams.description: Cross-sectional detail of the E.G.R. control valve showing internal diaphragm, spring, valve shaft, valve seat, and valve chamber.
wiring_and_connections: Vacuum port on top of diaphragm chamber
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Inspect diaphragm for leaks and valve stem for sticking or carbon deposits.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-16 Thermal vacuum valve
diagrams.description: Sectional views of the thermal vacuum valve at three temperature states: below 47-53°C (closed), 50-95°C (open), and above 92-98°C (closed).
wiring_and_connections: Port to throttle chamber
Port from E.G.R. control valve
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Wax element expands to open valve in normal range and closes valve above overheating threshold.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-17 B.P.T. valve
diagrams.description: Cross-sectional cutaway of the back-pressure transducer (B.P.T.) valve showing air filter, diaphragm, exhaust pressure port, and air bleed.
measurements_and_specs: Actuation pressure: 21 to 33 mmH2O (0.82 to 1.30 inH2O)
wiring_and_connections: Vacuum signal source line
Line to E.G.R. control valve
Exhaust pressure pickup line
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Diaphragm bleeds air to vent vacuum until sufficient exhaust backpressure pushes diaphragm closed.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-18 Vacuum delay valve
diagrams.description: Installation orientation and hose routing of the vacuum delay valve located between thermal vacuum valve (brown side) and B.P.T. valve (black side).
wiring_and_connections: Brown side connected toward thermal vacuum valve
Black side connected toward B.P.T. valve
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Pay strict attention to valve color orientation: Brown side faces thermal vacuum valve, Black side faces B.P.T. valve.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-19 Operation of vacuum delay valve
diagrams.description: Flow direction schematic of vacuum delay valve showing open umbrella flow toward thermal vacuum valve and restricted flow toward B.P.T. valve.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: One-way operation allows rapid flow during release and restricted flow during vacuum application.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-20 Removing E.G.R. control valve
diagrams.description: Removal of E.G.R. control valve nuts from intake manifold studs and vacuum hose disconnection.
wiring_and_connections: Flatten hose clip to disconnect vacuum hose
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Flatten clip connecting vacuum hose to E.G.R. control valve and remove hose by hand. Replace gasket upon reassembly.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-21 Removing B.P.T. valve
diagrams.description: Dismounting B.P.T. valve and control tube from intake manifold bracket.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Disconnect both vacuum hoses and unbolt B.P.T. valve from bracket.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-22 Removing thermal vacuum valve
diagrams.description: Removal and installation angle of thermal vacuum valve threaded into heater housing at 30 degree tilt angle.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Install thermal vacuum valve at a tilt angle of 30° as shown. Tighten to 2.2 kg-m (16 ft-lb) max. Drain coolant before removal.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-23 Checking thermal vacuum valve
diagrams.description: Checking vacuum presence at the hose disconnected from the thermal vacuum valve with finger while engine is revved.
wiring_and_connections: Hose disconnected at B.P.T. valve side
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Ensure throttle chamber vacuum is felt with finger when engine is warm (50 to 95°C) at 3,000-3,500 rpm.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-24 Checking B.P.T. valve
diagrams.description: Checking for vacuum at the disconnected hose from the B.P.T. valve leading to the E.G.R. valve at 3,000 to 3,500 rpm.
measurements_and_specs: Vacuum should be present when operating properly
wiring_and_connections: Hose disconnected at E.G.R. valve side
diagrams.mechanic_notes: If vacuum is not present at hose end during 3,000 to 3,500 rpm rev, replace B.P.T. valve.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-25 Checking E.G.R. control valve
diagrams.description: Feeling diaphragm of E.G.R. control valve with finger to confirm movement when revving engine from idle to 3,000-3,500 rpm.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Place finger under diaphragm to feel upward movement as engine is revved. If it does not move, replace valve.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-26 Checking thermal vacuum valve
diagrams.description: Blowing air orally through thermal vacuum valve submerged in heated water bath to verify opening and closing temperatures.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Do not allow water to get inside the thermal vacuum valve while heating.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-27 Checking vacuum delay valve
diagrams.description: Testing vacuum delay valve by blowing orally from each side while covering opposite port with finger.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Resistance should be greater when blowing from B.P.T. valve side with thermal valve side covered.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-28 Checking vacuum delay valve
diagrams.description: Submerging B.P.T. side port into cup of water while blowing through the other port to observe small air bubbles.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Small air bubbles indicate proper orifice flow. Avoid oil or dirt entering valve.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-29 Checking B.P.T. valve
diagrams.description: Testing B.P.T. valve leakage by applying pressure above 50 mmH2O to lower fitting while orally sucking vacuum port.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: If leakage occurs while sucking port back under applied pressure, replace valve.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-30 Checking E.G.R. control valve
diagrams.description: Testing E.G.R. valve diaphragm and seat by applying oral vacuum suction to vacuum hose port.
measurements_and_specs: Hold time: > 30 seconds after vacuum is cut off
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Valve must open fully and hold open position for more than 30 seconds after sealing hose.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-31 Cleaning E.G.R. control valve
diagrams.description: Cleaning carbon deposits from the E.G.R. control valve seating surface using a wire brush.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Clean seating surface and port with brush and compressed air. Check for wrinkles or deformation.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-32 Location of catalytic converter
diagrams.description: Vehicle side profile outline indicating catalytic converter position in the exhaust system under the floorpan.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: California models only. Positioned under passenger floor area in exhaust line.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-33 Operation of catalytic converter
diagrams.description: Flow diagram showing exhaust gases (HC, CO) mixing with excess air from exhaust manifold through catalytic converter bed to form CO2 and H2O.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Catalyst promotes oxidation of unburned hydrocarbons and carbon monoxide using residual excess oxygen.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-34 Removing catalytic converter
diagrams.description: Unbolting catalytic converter flange bolts connecting to front and rear exhaust tubes and lower heat shelter.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Never wet catalyzer with water or oil. Handle carefully to prevent internal ceramic fracture.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-35 Connecting emission adjuster
diagrams.description: Connecting the variable resistance emission adjuster tool to the disconnected water temperature sensor harness connector.
measurements_and_specs: Probe insertion depth: minimum 500 mm (19.69 in)
Pass criterion with #6 injector disconnected: < 1% CO
wiring_and_connections: Emission adjuster plugged into water temp sensor harness
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Simulate rich condition with emission adjuster, then cut #6 cylinder; CO must drop below 1% if catalyst is active.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-36 Floor temperature warning system circuit
diagrams.description: Schematic of floor temperature warning circuit showing battery, ignition switch, ignition relay, floor sensor relay, floor sensor, and floor temperature lamp.
wiring_and_connections: Ignition switch B, IG, S, A terminals
Relay coil and contact connections
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Floor sensor acts as normally closed contact at low temperature; opens when overheated, de-energizing relay and illuminating warning lamp.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-37 Location of floor sensor
diagrams.description: Chassis elevation outline showing location of the floor temperature sensor mounted above catalytic converter floor area.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Sensor is located under passenger floor carpet area above the exhaust pipe / catalytic converter section.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-38 Operation of floor sensor
diagrams.description: Internal bimetal mechanism of the floor sensor showing contacts closed (normal) and contacts open (overheated condition).
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Bimetallic disc snaps open at elevated floor temperatures, breaking relay coil ground.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-39 Removing floor sensor
diagrams.description: Interior passenger footwell view showing removal of floor protector and sensor screws.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove protective cover before loosening floor sensor mounting screws.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-40 Location of floor sensor relay
diagrams.description: Perspective drawing showing floor sensor relay and brake warning lamp check relay mounted beneath passenger seat.
wiring_and_connections: Relay harness plug under passenger seat
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove front passenger seat to access the floor sensor relay on seat bracket.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-41 Location of floor temperature lamp
diagrams.description: Dashboard center console view showing location of FLOOR TEMP warning light lens on heater/vent finisher panel.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Remove center console instrument finisher panel to replace bulb or warning unit.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-42 Wiring diagram of floor temperature warning system
diagrams.description: Complete schematic diagram of floor temperature warning system showing wire colors, connector pinouts, battery, fusible links, starting motor, ignition switch, fuse box, ignition relay, floor sensor relay, floor sensor, and floor temperature warning lamp.
wiring_and_connections: WR (White/Red)
WB (White/Black)
BW (Black/White)
RB (Red/Black)
BY (Black/Yellow)
BR (Black/Red)
B (Black ground)
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Shows all multi-pin harness connectors, wire color coding, and relay pin numbers for floor temperature warning circuitry.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-43 Floor temperature warning lamp ON with ignition switch in \"START\" position
diagrams.description: Current flow path through circuit diagram when ignition switch is in START position, proving bulb bulb-check functionality.
wiring_and_connections: BY line energized from STA terminal to illuminate warning lamp during cranking
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Heavy lines trace circuit from starter terminal through warning lamp to ground during cranking.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-44 Floor temperature warning lamp ON with floor sensor turned OFF
diagrams.description: Current flow path when floor sensor bimetal opens (OFF state), de-energizing relay and routing 12V through relay normally-closed contacts to warning lamp.
wiring_and_connections: Current flow traced through de-energized relay contacts to lamp
diagrams.mechanic_notes: When sensor heats above 115°C, its internal contact opens, cutting relay coil ground; relay returns to NC position and lights bulb.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-45 Checking floor sensor relay
diagrams.description: Terminal pin numbering and internal coil/switch diagram of the floor sensor relay for bench continuity testing.
measurements_and_specs: Terminals 2-4: NC contact (Yes normal, No energized)
Terminals 1-3: NO contact (No normal, Yes energized)
wiring_and_connections: 12V DC applied across coil terminals 5 and 6
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Use fused test lead when energizing terminals 5 and 6.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-46 Schematic drawing of evaporative emission control system
diagrams.description: Chassis perspective view showing complete evaporative plumbing: fuel tank, filler cap, separator, vapor lines, check valve, and canister.
components: Fuel filler cap with vacuum relief valve

callouts.5: Fuel filler cap with vacuum relief valve

wiring_and_connections: Plumbing lines connecting rear separator, underbody vapor line, and engine compartment canister
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Fuel tank is sealed with a vacuum relief filler cap. Vapors pass through liquid/vapor separator and check valve to canister.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-47 Evaporative emission control system (Fuel vapor flow when engine is at rest or at idling)
diagrams.description: Functional flow schematic at rest or idle showing vapor trapped in activated carbon while purge control valve remains closed.
components: Fuel filler cap with vacuum relief valve

callouts.2: Fuel filler cap with vacuum relief valve

diagrams.mechanic_notes: At rest or idle, purge control valve diaphragm spring holds valve closed so vapors are retained in activated carbon.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-48 Evaporative emission control system (Fuel vapor flow when engine is running)
diagrams.description: Functional flow schematic showing purge control valve opened by port vacuum during running conditions, admitting fresh air through canister bottom and purging vapors to intake manifold.
wiring_and_connections: Vacuum signal line to throttle chamber port
Purge line to intake manifold port
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Throttle vacuum lifts diaphragm against spring, pulling fresh air through canister bottom filter and purging absorbed vapors into engine.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-49 Checking evaporative emission control system
diagrams.description: Apparatus setup for pressure testing vapor vent line, separator, and tank using manometer, 3-way connector cock, and hand air pump.
measurements_and_specs: Max allowable pressure drop: 25 mmH2O (0.98 inH2O) over 2.5 minutes
wiring_and_connections: Manometer tee connected to disconnected vent line at canister
diagrams.mechanic_notes: If pressure drops immediately, filler cap or vent hoses leak. If pressure does not drop when cap removed, line is clogged.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-50 Checking carbon canister purge control valve
diagrams.description: Inhaling oral suction on disconnected rubber hose to canister purge control valve diaphragm port to check for diaphragm leakage.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: There must be no leakage when inhaling on hose. If leaking, replace diaphragm kit.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-51 Carbon canister purge control valve
diagrams.description: Exploded view of the purge control valve assembly on top of the carbon canister.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Diaphragm kit consists of retainer, diaphragm, and spring.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-52 Replacing carbon canister filter
diagrams.description: Hand removal and replacement of the fibrous bottom filter pad of the carbon canister.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Filter pad is easily pulled out from bottom recess of canister body when dirty.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-53 Fuel filler cap
diagrams.description: Cross-sectional cutaway of fuel filler cap vacuum relief valve mechanism showing internal spring and sealing gasket.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Oral inhalation should produce slight resistance then click as valve opens. Replace cap if clogged or free-leaking.

diagrams.caption: Fig. EC-54 Checking fuel check valve
diagrams.description: Cross-sectional flow diagram of two-way fuel check valve showing differential resistance between fuel tank side and engine side.
diagrams.mechanic_notes: Air blown into engine side should flow freely toward tank; air blown into tank side should show considerable resistance.

troubleshooting.symptom: No hissing noise or vacuum felt at P.C.V. valve inlet at idle
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Clogged or defective P.C.V. valve, or obstructed ventilation hose
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Clean or replace P.C.V. valve; clean ventilation hoses with compressed air or replace

troubleshooting.symptom: B.C.D.D. circuit test shows no continuity at complete stop (M/T)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Disconnected connector, faulty amplifier, faulty speed detecting switch, or faulty B.C.D.D. solenoid valve
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check connectors, test and replace faulty unit

troubleshooting.symptom: B.C.D.D. circuit test shows voltage (not 0V) at speed > 16 km/h (M/T)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Disconnected connector, burned fuse, faulty amplifier, faulty solenoid valve, or faulty speed detecting switch
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Inspect fuse and wiring, test components and replace if defective

troubleshooting.symptom: B.C.D.D. circuit test shows 0V in 'N' or 'P' position (A/T)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Disconnected connector, faulty solenoid valve, or faulty inhibitor switch
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Inspect wiring, check inhibitor switch adjustment or replace faulty solenoid/switch

troubleshooting.symptom: B.C.D.D. circuit resistance not 15 to 28 ohms in gear (A/T)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Poor connector connection, faulty B.C.D.D. solenoid valve, or faulty inhibitor switch
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Repair connector connection or replace faulty solenoid/inhibitor switch

troubleshooting.symptom: B.C.D.D. solenoid valve does not click when electrified
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Defective solenoid valve coil or open circuit
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check continuity with tester; replace solenoid valve if discontinuity is detected

troubleshooting.symptom: Speedometer amplifier tester pointer does not deflect when ignition is turned ON
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Faulty amplifier (assuming solenoid and speed switch are intact)
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Replace amplifier located at rear of speedometer

troubleshooting.symptom: Engine speed cannot be decreased to idling during B.C.D.D. pressure adjustment
troubleshooting.probable_cause: B.C.D.D. operating pressure incorrectly adjusted (too high on vacuum)
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Turn adjusting nut (California) or screw (Non-California) as directed in 1/4 or 1/2 turn increments until properly set

troubleshooting.symptom: Vacuum present at thermal vacuum valve hose below 47°C (117°F)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Faulty or stuck-open thermal vacuum valve
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Replace thermal vacuum valve

troubleshooting.symptom: No vacuum at thermal vacuum valve hose at 50 to 95°C (122 to 203°F) and 3,000-3,500 rpm
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Faulty or stuck-closed thermal vacuum valve, or clogged vacuum port
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Clean passage or replace thermal vacuum valve

troubleshooting.symptom: No vacuum at B.P.T. valve hose to E.G.R. valve at 3,000-3,500 rpm
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Faulty B.P.T. valve diaphragm or air bleed leak
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Replace B.P.T. valve

troubleshooting.symptom: E.G.R. control valve diaphragm does not lift at 3,000-3,500 rpm
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Sticking E.G.R. valve spindle, ruptured diaphragm, or lack of vacuum signal
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Clean valve seating surface/spindle; test diaphragm hold time; replace E.G.R. valve if defective

troubleshooting.symptom: B.P.T. valve leaks during oral suction test under 50 mmH2O pressure
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Ruptured internal diaphragm in B.P.T. valve
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Replace B.P.T. valve

troubleshooting.symptom: E.G.R. control valve does not remain open for > 30 seconds after vacuum cut off
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Ruptured or leaking E.G.R. valve diaphragm
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Replace E.G.R. control valve

troubleshooting.symptom: CO percentage is greater than 1% with #6 injector disconnected (catalytic converter test)
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Exhausted or damaged catalytic converter
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Replace catalytic converter

troubleshooting.symptom: Floor temperature warning lamp does not light on START
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Burned-out warning lamp bulb or open wiring from starter switch terminal
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Replace bulb or repair wiring from starter 'STA' circuit

troubleshooting.symptom: Floor temperature warning lamp stays lit at normal operating temperatures
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Defective floor sensor (contacts stuck open), faulty floor sensor relay, or short in wiring harness
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Test floor sensor continuity, test relay on bench with 12V, trace wiring and replace defective part

troubleshooting.symptom: Floor temperature warning lamp flashes frequently with power loss and engine vibration
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Misfiring or unburned fuel causing catalytic converter overheating; ignition or EFI fault
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Check ignition AMP, distributor, coil, HT cables, spark plugs, EFI injectors, B.C.D.D., and air cleaner

troubleshooting.symptom: Evaporative manometer pressure drops > 25 mmH2O in 2.5 minutes
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Leak in fuel tank, vapor-liquid separator, vent lines, or fuel filler cap seal
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Inspect connections and hoses for cracks; inspect or replace fuel filler cap

troubleshooting.symptom: Evaporative manometer pressure does not drop to zero when filler cap is removed
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Stuffy or pinched vapor vent hose
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Clear obstruction or replace vent hose

troubleshooting.symptom: Carbon canister purge control valve leaks upon oral suction
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Cracked or dislocated purge control valve diaphragm
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Remove top cover and replace diaphragm kit (retainer, diaphragm, spring)

troubleshooting.symptom: Fuel filler cap vacuum relief valve does not click or offers no resistance upon inhalation
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Clogged, jammed, or leaking vacuum relief valve mechanism
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Replace fuel filler cap assembly

troubleshooting.symptom: Fuel check valve offers no resistance or does not flow toward tank smoothly
troubleshooting.probable_cause: Defective internal check valve disc or spring
troubleshooting.corrective_action: Replace fuel check valve
